leads.summary: New migration reverses Remove Preinstalls on existing users
leads.consequence: For a user who ran Remove Preinstalls, the migration runs omarchy-refresh-applications unconditionally. That command copies the removed web app and TUI launchers back (13 stock entries match the remover predicates), then recreates removed mise-backed command wrappers. The packages removed by Remove Preinstalls are not reinstalled, while ~/.local/state/omarchy/preinstalls-removed stays set: removed apps return to the launcher (some cannot run), the menu still offers Restore and its opt-out state remains inconsistent. A successful refresh marks the migration done, so this persists until users remove the entries again. Restrict this migration to updating imv.desktop, or make refresh honor the opt-out marker as open PR #9703 proposes.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (N1 preinstalls case); corroboration, published as N1

leads.summary: Unrelated personal desktop entries and command wrappers are overwritten by the imv migration
leads.consequence: Instead of copying only imv.desktop, the migration's callee overwrites every stock-named user desktop entry (including custom Discord.desktop or HEY.desktop) with cp, and runs install/user/mise.sh. omarchy-mise-install first deletes any pre-existing ~/.local/bin/<command>, even an executable chosen by the user, then writes Omarchy's own wrapper. Examples include codex, claude, gh, pi and 13 more unconditional names, with cursor-agent/muse conditional. No backup or provenance guard is made. On success the runner writes the marker, so restoring custom files requires manual repair. Scope the migration to the single image viewer entry and its desktop cache; do not run the global installer for this MIME change. Open PR #13243 independently guards against clobbering a user's own wrapper but is not merged here.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (N1 ordinary-user case); merged into N1. PR #13243 reference verified via gh, not published

leads.summary: Related open PR #13123 conflicts with the newly added image defaults and its test
leads.consequence: #13123 changes the six existing image defaults to imv-dir.desktop and adds test/shell.d/mimeapps-test.sh enforcing that all image/ defaults use imv-dir.desktop and none use imv.desktop. These four new defaults use imv.desktop. Three-way merge against the shared 61079e base produced conflict markers around every image row, not an automatic clean merge. Simply keeping both sets by taking #13123's six old rows and this PR's four new rows leaves its test failing. Coordinate the four new defaults and the test with #13123 when resolving; imv 5.0.1 ships imv-dir.desktop and declares HEIF, AVIF and JXL. GitHub's current mergeable for #13123 is UNKNOWN, so this is a directly reproduced file conflict, not a claim about GitHub's final merge result.
leads.triage: factual; coordinator verified gh pr diff 13123 (imv-dir defaults + mimeapps-test.sh rejecting image/*=imv.desktop); Opus draft-check also confirmed; published as Related open PR note (N2)

leads.summary: Potential remaining generic xdg-open gap for HEIF/HEIC image sequences
leads.consequence: The shipped file/libmagic 5.48 recognizes HEVC image-sequence brands hevc/hevx as image/heic-sequence and other HEIF sequence brands as image/heif-sequence. shared-mime-info aliases those names to image/heif for GIO, but xdg-utils 1.2.1 checks the literal MIME key on the generic route. Neither new default nor the imv desktop entry includes the sequence names. Thus generic xdg-open may still choose another application for HEIF sequences. This is a hypothesis, not a recommendation to register them yet: first confirm imv 5.0.1 can decode and display actual HEIF image-sequence samples (the backend reads the primary image handle rather than an explicit sequence API), and confirm sequence support is within the intended PR scope.
leads.triage: hypothesis (HEIF sequences); Opus lists as untested; not published as a finding, kept as Test scope limit

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up to the [earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12368#issuecomment-5832221110) and the [author's reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12368#issuecomment-5834354556), checked at head `22711ef`. Both earlier points are resolved. The new migration fixes GIO registration, but it does so by rerunning a much broader command, and that command was the earlier review's own suggestion. A narrower migration is suggested below.

**Verified:** routing at the new head, isolated fixture with a Hyprland session value, stub handlers, a competing viewer claiming every type, and real `heif-enc`, `avifenc` and `cjxl` output:

```text
sample (file --mime-type)          earlier head             this head
                                   xdg-open / gio open      xdg-open / gio open
.heic, heic brand (image/heic)     other viewer / imv       imv / imv
.heif, heic brand (image/heic)     other viewer / imv       imv / imv
.heif, mif1 brand (image/heif)     imv / imv                imv / imv
.avif, .jxl, .png                  imv / imv                imv / imv
```

- **`.heic` through `xdg-open` (earlier finding): resolved.** `image/heic=imv.desktop` in `default/applications/mimeapps.list` and `image/heic;` in the `MimeType` line both route it to imv. `gio mime image/heic` reports imv as the default.
- **Existing installs (earlier Optional note): resolved.** In a simulated existing install (old user-level launchers, new system defaults), imv was the default but missing from GIO's registered and recommended lists. After `migrations/1789706522.sh`, imv is registered and recommended for AVIF, HEIF, HEIC and JXL.
- `default/applications/mimeapps.list` is installed as the package-owned `/usr/share/applications/mimeapps.list`, so the new defaults reach existing installs through the package upgrade, and the migration rightly leaves it alone. `desktop-file-validate` reports the new `imv.desktop` clean.

### The migration restores removed preinstall launchers and resets edited stock launchers and wrappers

`migrations/1789706522.sh` runs `omarchy-refresh-applications`, which does much more than refresh `imv.desktop`:

```text
omarchy-refresh-applications
├─ cp applications/*.desktop → ~/.local/share/applications   (16 launchers: 11 web apps, 2 TUIs, foot, imv, mpv)
├─ install/user/mise.sh → omarchy-mise-install × 19           (2 only when missing; rm -f ~/.local/bin/<name>, then write a mise wrapper)
└─ update-desktop-database
```

The same command is the restore step of `omarchy-install-preinstalls`. The per-tool wrapper migrations (for example `1785617047`) skip when `~/.local/state/omarchy/preinstalls-removed` exists; this migration has no such check. Observed in an isolated synthetic home, with the migration run under `bash -euo pipefail` as the migration runner does and `mise` stubbed:

- **After Remove > Preinstalls:** 13 removed launchers came back (Basecamp, Discord, Disk Usage, Docker, the four Google apps, HEY, WhatsApp, X, YouTube, Zoom), and the refresh wrote all 19 mise wrappers into `~/.local/bin`, including the ones Remove > Preinstalls deletes. Removed packages are not reinstalled. The marker stays, so the menu still hides Remove > Preinstalls while the launchers are back.
- **Ordinary install:** a single web app launcher the user had deleted (`X.desktop`) came back, a line appended to `mpv.desktop` was lost, and a user-owned `~/.local/bin/claude` symlink was replaced by a mise wrapper.

**Impact:** every existing install reruns this on update. Anyone who removed preinstalls gets their launchers and wrappers back, and any stock launcher or wrapper a user deleted or changed is reset, from a change that only needs imv's MIME registration refreshed.

**Suggested change:** refresh only the imv launcher, as migration `1787580187` does for `Docker.desktop`:

```bash
echo "Refresh imv launcher so it registers for AVIF, HEIF, HEIC, and JXL"

dest="$HOME/.local/share/applications/imv.desktop"
if [[ -f $dest ]]; then
  cp "$OMARCHY_PATH/applications/imv.desktop" "$dest"
  update-desktop-database "$HOME/.local/share/applications"
fi
```

In the same fixture this gave the same GIO registration and routing as the current migration and changed only `imv.desktop` and `mimeinfo.cache`. It left removed preinstalls removed, changed nothing on a second run, and did nothing when the user had deleted `imv.desktop` (the packaged imv entry still covered the types). `update-desktop-database` is needed: with the copy alone, GIO still left imv out of the registered list. Open PR #9703 proposes making the refresh command itself honor the preinstalls opt-out, which would address the first case at the source, but not the overwritten launchers and wrappers.

**Correction to the earlier review:** it suggested a migration running `omarchy-refresh-applications`, without accounting for these side effects. It also said earlier `applications/*.desktop` changes shipped without a migration. That was inaccurate: #8056 changed `Docker.desktop` and shipped migration `1787580187`, which refreshes only that file. (The unguarded refresh does have one precedent, migration `1786183928` for a mise wrapper change.)

**Related open PR:** #13123 switches the image defaults to `imv-dir.desktop` and adds `test/shell.d/mimeapps-test.sh`, which fails if any `image/*` default points at `imv.desktop`. The four new lines here use `imv.desktop`, so whichever PR lands second needs to align them.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Follow-up source review of head `22711ef` (rebased since the earlier review) and the migration's callees, plus the xdg-utils 1.2.1, file 5.48, GLib 2.88.3 and imv 5.0.1 sources, with shared-mime-info 2.5.1 and desktop-file-utils 0.28 as installed tools. Routing and migration effects were tested in isolated command-only fixtures with a synthetic home, stub handlers and a stubbed `mise`; the mif1-brand `.heif` sample is `heif-enc` output with its brand patched; no real session or imv window was opened. Decoding was not retested (the new commit does not change it; imv's libheif and libjxl linkage was rechecked). HEIF/HEIC image sequences were not tested.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
